130.title: postgres-payments: enable slow-query logging via parameter group in postgres_payments.tf
130.body: postgres_payments.tf now defines a parameter group for the payments cluster with log_min_duration_statement=250 and log_lock_waits=on, attached in the same apply. We've had almost no visibility into what's actually slow behind the checkout latency dashboards, and the pg_stat snapshots we grab by hand don't survive a failover. Logs flow to the existing payments log group, so the slow-query panel can start pointing at real statements instead of guesswork. Testing: terraform plan reviewed and applied to staging; confirmed slow statements show up in the log group within a couple of minutes.

131.title: inventory: include SKU and stock level in OutOfStock raised by reserve
131.body: reserve() used to raise a bare OutOfStock, so every upstream log just said 'reservation failed' and support had to go ask the caller which SKU they meant. The exception now carries the SKU, requested quantity, and what was actually on hand, and the message renders those fields so it's readable in raw logs. No change to when the error fires — same condition, just more context. This should cut a step out of most stock-shortage tickets.

132.title: pricing: quantize PricingService.total_for to cents
132.body: total_for was returning whatever the discount pipeline handed it, so a 12.345 subtotal could leave the service unrounded and get rounded differently by every caller. PricingService.total_for now quantizes to cents with ROUND_HALF_UP before returning, and the docstring documents it. Callers that still round on their side are unaffected — they're just rounding an already-rounded number. Testing: added half-cent boundary cases to the pricing suite.

133.title: cart: add DELETE /carts/{cart_id} backed by CartService.clear
133.body: Carts could only be filled, never emptied — new_cart and get_cart covered the happy path, and the nightly cleanup job was the only thing touching abandoned ones. This adds CartService.clear plus a DELETE /carts/{cart_id} route that delegates to the store's clear and reuses get_cart's not-found path, so a missing cart 404s instead of blowing up. Cart.clear drops the line items in place and bumps the updated_at stamp that store __init__ initializes, keeping the TTL job honest.

166.title: inventory: make InventoryService.reserve check availability in-transaction
166.body: InventoryService.reserve checked availability and wrote the decrement in separate transactions, so a rejected reservation could still bump the counter until the cleanup job ran. The check now lives inside the same transaction as the decrement in app.py, and rejections raise a typed ReservationError instead of a bare 409. Also logs sku and requested quantity at debug on the rejected path. Testing: unit cases in tests/inventory/test_reserve.py cover oversell and concurrent reserve.

167.title: postgres-payments: set backup retention and maintenance window in postgres_payments.tf
167.body: postgres_payments.tf sets backup_retention_period to 14 days (was 1), pins the maintenance window to Sunday 04:00 UTC, and adds the service/env tags the alerting stack expects so disk-usage and replica-lag alarms route to the payments pager instead of the default channel. The replica-lag metric was previously declared inline in two places; both now reference a single local.

168.title: payments-api: type PaymentsService.capture results and share refund validation
168.body: PaymentsService.capture returned the raw gateway payload and every caller parsed it slightly differently. This adds a CaptureResult dataclass and converts at the boundary in app.py. In handlers/refund.py, refund() now reuses the amount validation from PaymentsService.refund instead of its own regex, and logs the gateway reference at warning when a refund is rejected for exceeding the captured amount. Testing: added cases for malformed gateway payloads and refund amounts above the capture.

169.title: search: incremental segment rebuilds in build_index
169.body: build_index rebuilt every segment on each run, which left search results stale for up to 20 minutes after a deploy. indexer.py now tracks a per-segment updated_at watermark and rewrites only segments whose source rows changed. SearchService.search emits latency and result-count metrics via the existing metrics module, and app.py gains a readiness endpoint that reports not-ready until the first build completes. Testing: integration test builds a two-segment index, touches one row, and asserts only one segment is rewritten.

170.title: kafka: retune topic partitions and retention in kafka.tf
170.body: Bumps order-events to 24 partitions in kafka.tf so the inventory consumer can keep pace during backfills, and drops clickstream retention from 7 days to 3 — we never replay past 48h anyway. Consumer-lag alarms move into the standard metrics block instead of the hand-rolled JSON that lives in the wiki.

171.title: auth: constant-time hash check and cleaner login logs in AuthService
171.body: AuthService.login was comparing stored hashes with ==, so I swapped it for hmac.compare_digest — mostly hygiene, but it also kills the timing weirdness on mismatched lengths. Failed logins now log one generic reason plus a request id instead of three different messages that made the dashboards noisy, and the session cookie set in app.py finally gets Secure and SameSite=Lax flags.

172.title: search: fix build_index temp-dir cleanup and add search pagination
172.body: Follow-up to the incremental indexer: if build_index died mid-merge it left the temp segment directory behind, and the next run then skipped that shard entirely — found this while chasing why one shard was a day old. Cleanup now happens in a finally block in indexer.py. SearchService.search also takes an offset/limit pair so the results page can paginate instead of pulling 500 hits, with app.py passing the params straight through. Testing: regression test kills build_index mid-merge and asserts the next run rebuilds the shard.

173.title: postgres-payments: deletion protection and performance insights on the payments primary
173.body: Small follow-up to the backup-window change: postgres_payments.tf now sets deletion_protection on the primary and pins final_snapshot_identifier, so a stray apply can't drop the payments database without an explicit untaint. Also enables performance insights with 7-day retention and wires its load metrics into the existing dashboard definition rather than a separate panel.

150.title: postgres-payments: manage slow-query log export and disk alarms in postgres_payments.tf
150.body:
Both of these settings were last changed by hand in the console, so plan output has been showing drift for weeks. This brings the slow-query log export and a free-storage alarm under infra/terraform/postgres_payments.tf so the next apply is a no-op instead of a surprise. I kept the alarm threshold where ops had it set. No instance or storage settings are modified.

Testing: terraform plan against staging shows only the two new resources and no in-place updates.

151.title: refunds: reject invalid amounts up front in start_refund
151.body:
start_refund currently accepts whatever amount and currency it is given and lets the background job discover the problem, which is how we end up with cryptic entries in the refunds dead-letter list. This pulls the amount/currency validation into start_refund so obviously bad requests fail synchronously with a readable error. Valid refunds behave exactly as before, and I left the job-side checks in place as a backstop.

Testing: added unit cases for zero, negative, and currency-mismatched amounts against start_refund.

152.title: auth: share one error serializer between AuthService.login and oauth.login
152.body: The two login paths have drifted: AuthService.login in app.py returns {error: msg} while oauth.login in oauth.py returns bare strings, so the frontend keeps a second parser around just for OAuth failures. This routes both through a shared serializer in oauth.py that emits stable {code, message} payloads. Successful logins, token issuance, and session handling are untouched.

153.title: cart: get_cart raises CartNotFound instead of returning an empty cart
153.body:
get_cart was silently constructing a fresh cart for unknown ids, which meant a stale tab could 'recover' a cart that was never theirs and check out with nothing in it. Now only new_cart creates carts, and get_cart raises CartNotFound, mapped to a 404 in the route layer. Existing carts are unaffected, but this is a behavior change so the frontend folks should confirm their error handling.

Testing: unit tests cover get_cart for a missing id and for a cart created via new_cart.

154.title: email-sender: per-send outcome logging in send_email and outbox count in clear
154.body: send_email gave us nothing back — a bounced address only surfaced when someone complained. It now logs one info line per message with the template, recipient domain, and outcome, plus a counter so we can graph delivery by provider. clear() also logs how many pending messages it dropped, so an unexpected flush leaves a trail in the logs instead of vanishing quietly.

155.title: checkout: tighten fresh_state scoping and split confirmation assertions into their own test
155.body:
fresh_state was module-scoped, so test_place_order_happy_path could leave order rows behind that later tests leaned on without declaring it. This makes it function-scoped and clears the orders table between tests. I also moved the confirmation-content assertions out of the happy path into test_place_order_confirmation_mentions_order, which previously just duplicated them, and added the missing-order-number case there. test_place_order_empty_cart_fails needed no changes once state was isolated.

Testing: pytest services/checkout/tests/test_place_order.py is green locally, including the new case.

156.title: web-frontend: render_checkout preserves input focus during total updates
156.body: render_checkout rebuilds the entire checkout DOM whenever the cart total changes, so anyone typing their address loses focus mid-field every time a discount recalculates. This patches only the summary section in place and leaves the form subtree alone, keeping focus and cursor position where they were. The payment step markup is unchanged.

157.title: api-gateway: attach bucket context to RateLimited and count rejections in check_limit
157.body: Every limited request looked the same in the access logs because check_limit discarded the reason. The RateLimited exception now carries the bucket key and the remaining window, and check_limit increments a rejected_total counter we can slice by route. I also made reset log the bucket it clears so manual flushes are auditable instead of invisible.

182.title: auth: constant-time comparison in AuthService.login
182.body:
The password check in AuthService.login compared digests with ==, which leaks timing information on failure. Swapped it for hmac.compare_digest and pulled the check into a small helper so the upcoming MFA path can reuse it. Also added a debug log of the auth method on success to make password vs. SSO logins distinguishable in prod.

Testing: Unit tests cover mismatched and truncated digests; full auth suite passes.

183.title: kafka: make replication factor a variable in kafka.tf
183.body: Replication factor was hardcoded at 3 for every topic in kafka.tf, which staging doesn't need. This makes it a variable (default 3, staging set to 2), pins min.insync.replicas to match, and declares the DLQ topics that were previously created by hand. Prod topic configs are unchanged — plan came back clean.

184.title: identity-api: drop duplicate verify_refresh_token from IdentityService
184.body:
app.py carried a second copy of verify_refresh_token inside IdentityService that had drifted from tokens.py and skipped the expiry check, so expired refresh tokens were accepted by the refresh route. Deleted the copy; issue_refresh_token and verify_refresh_token now both live in tokens.py and IdentityService just calls them. Token format is unchanged — tokens issued before this PR verify exactly as before.

Testing: Added a regression test for the expired-token path and ran the identity suite.

185.title: postgres-ledger: enable deletion protection in postgres_ledger.tf
185.body: The ledger database is the one Postgres instance left without deletion_protection, and a mis-targeted apply is all it would take to lose the source of truth. This enables deletion protection plus a final snapshot on the ledger instance and brings its tags in line with the other databases in terraform. Both show as in-place changes in the plan, but I'd like a second pair of eyes on the apply since this database gets no do-overs.

186.title: postgres-ledger: export slow query logs in postgres_ledger.tf
186.body:
Tracking down the slow nightly ledger rollup meant SSH-ing to the primary and grepping logs by hand. This wires up slow-query log export in postgres_ledger.tf via the existing parameter group, so statements over 500ms land in the central log search like every other database. The threshold is a variable now, so it's easy to tune per environment.

Testing: Applied to staging; slow-query entries show up in the log search within a minute.

187.title: payments-api: structured outcome logging in capture
187.body:
The capture handler emitted one unstructured log line per request, so telling an approved capture from a declined one meant parsing prose. capture now logs a structured event with order id, amount, currency, and outcome, and increments a payments_capture_outcome counter the payments dashboard can graph directly. Request and response contracts are untouched.

Testing: Unit tests assert the logged fields for both approved and declined captures.

188.title: postgres-payments: storage autoscaling in postgres_payments.tf
188.body: Storage on the payments database was fixed at 200 GB and the last big backfill pushed it close enough to the ceiling that we had to resize by hand mid-run. postgres_payments.tf now uses storage autoscaling with a 500 GB limit, and I enabled performance insights at 7-day retention so the next growth question answers itself from the console. Plan shows in-place changes only, no restart.

189.title: email-sender: cache compiled templates in send_email
189.body:
While poking at the welcome flow I noticed EmailSenderService.send_email recompiles the template on every single call, so a batch of password resets re-renders the same file over and over. This adds a small module-level cache in app.py keyed by template name, with a recompile on miss as the fallback. Rendered output is byte-for-byte identical to before.

Testing: Added a test that a second send_email call hits the cache, plus a smoke send to the staging inbox.

142.title: identity-api: rotate refresh tokens in verify_refresh_token/issue_refresh_token
142.body: verify_refresh_token() currently accepts the same refresh token indefinitely, which defeats the point of rotation. This change marks a token as consumed on verify and has issue_refresh_token() mint its replacement within the same family, so replaying an old token invalidates the whole set. IdentityService in app.py now tracks the family id alongside the token hash and revokes the family on reuse.

143.title: postgres-main: enable slow-query logging and extend backups in postgres_main.tf
143.body: After the last slow-morning incident I got tired of guessing which queries were the problem. This adds a parameter group to postgres_main.tf with log_min_duration_statement at 500ms and log_lock_waits on, so slow queries and lock waits actually show up in logs. Also bumps backup retention to 14 days and pins a Sunday morning maintenance window while I was in there.

144.title: identity-api: return stable 401s from verify_refresh_token with audit logging
144.body: Malformed or expired refresh tokens currently bubble out of verify_refresh_token() as a 500 with a stack trace, which is both wrong and noisy. This catches decode and expiry errors in IdentityService and returns a 401 with a stable error code, plus a warning-level log line carrying the failure reason. I checked with the client team that they already handle the new code gracefully.

145.title: payment-router: hot-reload rules in PaymentRouter.route and add clear()
145.body: PaymentRouter.__init__ froze the rule table at startup, so every routing tweak meant a full deploy. route() now consults a rules object that a small management endpoint can swap at runtime, and the table keeps its priority ordering across swaps. Also added clear() to reset the router to defaults, which stops tests from leaking rule state into each other.

146.title: kafka: extend events topic retention and add compacted snapshot topic in kafka.tf
146.body: Retention on the events topic was 24h, and it bit us twice this month when a consumer was down longer than a day and lost the window. This bumps retention.ms to 7 days in kafka.tf and adds a new compacted topic for the snapshot stream, so consumers can recover from the last record per key instead of scrolling back through everything.

147.title: payments-api: add expiry sweep and hit/miss counters to the make_key cache
147.body: Entries written by store() never expire, so the cache grows for the life of the process. This adds a timestamp to stored entries, lets clear() drop anything older than the TTL, and wires get() to record hit/miss counters so we can finally see what the cache is actually doing. Also adds type hints to match the rest of the package.

148.title: ledger: switch LedgerEntry to Decimal and capture publishes in FakeBus
148.body: LedgerEntry.amount was a float, and rounding drift showed up whenever a summary added a few thousand entries. This switches the field to Decimal with fixed scale at two places. FakeBus.publish now records everything it sends, so tests can assert on message order and contents instead of poking at bus internals.

149.title: payments-api: structured logging and latency metrics in capture()
149.body: capture() logged via bare print statements and collapsed every failure into one generic error, which made the handler logs close to useless during incidents. This adds structured fields (order_id, provider, amount), a duration histogram around the provider call, and distinct exception types so validation problems read differently from provider outages when you're on call.

190.title: postgres-payments: export slow-query logs from postgres_payments.tf to the logging pipeline
190.body: Adds a parameter group in infra/terraform/postgres_payments.tf setting log_min_duration_statement to 500ms and routes the postgres log type to the shared log sink. Payments queries currently only show up in ad-hoc psql sessions; this puts them next to everything else we already search. No other instance settings touched.

191.title: redis-cache: enable AOF persistence and allkeys-lru in redis-cache values.yaml
191.body: Sets appendonly yes with appendfsync everysec and maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru in infra/helm/redis-cache/values.yaml. Everything in this cache is rebuildable, so losing it to a pod reschedule was more annoying than dangerous — checkout_sessions just get re-warmed. Also pinned the chart version while I was in there so the next upgrade isn't a surprise.

192.title: identity-api: stamp kid headers in issue_refresh_token and enforce them in verify_refresh_token
192.body:
issue_refresh_token now signs refresh tokens with an explicit kid header, and verify_refresh_token rejects any token whose kid isn't in KEYRING. Previously both signing keys were tried in order, which blocked ever rotating the legacy key out of the ring. IdentityService now maps InvalidTokenError from verify_refresh_token to a 401 with a re-auth hint, matching what the docs already claim.

Testing: unit tests cover mint-then-verify round-trips with both key ids plus a tampered kid; existing suite green.

193.title: checkout: share cart setup via fresh_state across test_place_order tests
193.body:
The three place_order tests each rolled their own teardown, and test_place_order_empty_cart_fails was leaving rows behind that made test_place_order_happy_path flaky depending on run order. This centralizes setup/cleanup in the fresh_state fixture and adds test_place_order_confirmation_mentions_order covering the confirmation copy (order number plus first line item). retry.py itself is untouched — tests only.

Testing: pytest services/checkout/tests/test_place_order.py — 3 passed, run 20x locally in both orders.

194.title: web-frontend: fix currency symbol in render_checkout for non-default locales
194.body: render_checkout was formatting the order total with the server default locale, so shoppers with a EUR profile saw 'US$ 54.00' on the summary and tax lines. It now reads the profile currency set by the session middleware and only falls back to the default when unset. No template changes.

195.title: refunds: validate amount against original payment in start_refund
195.body:
start_refund currently forwards whatever amount it's given and lets the payment provider reject over-refunds downstream, which surfaces to support as a generic 500. It now compares the request against the original payment total and raises RefundAmountError with both amounts in the message, so RefundsService can return a 422 the CSR UI can actually render.

Testing: new cases in tests/test_refunds.py for under/over/exact amounts; full suite green.

196.title: web-frontend: send no-store headers from WebFrontend for /checkout
196.body:
WebFrontend now sets Cache-Control: no-store on the render_checkout route in services/web_frontend/app.py. The back button was showing a stale cart total after the cart changed in another tab, and two support tickets last week traced to exactly that. Marketing pages keep their existing caching headers.

Testing: curl -i against /checkout shows the header; screenshot diff of the page is unchanged.

197.title: postgres-ledger: enable deletion protection and 14-day backups in postgres_ledger.tf
197.body: Turns on deletion_protection and extends the automated backup retention window from 3 to 14 days in infra/terraform/postgres_ledger.tf. Ledger is the only store we can't rebuild from an upstream system, and the current settings didn't reflect that. Apply needs the maintenance window; I'll run it after the nightly ledger batch finishes.

222.title: payment-router: read provider order from config in PaymentRouter.__init__
222.body: PaymentRouter.__init__ hardcodes the provider ordering, so route() always tries the same provider first and rebalancing traffic means a deploy. This moves the ordering into a config mapping that __init__ reads once at startup, and route() walks providers in that order. Defaults match the old hardcoded sequence, so nothing changes on the happy path.

223.title: api-gateway: emit Retry-After on RateLimited responses
223.body: RateLimited responses currently tell clients they are throttled but not when the window clears, so clients poll blindly until check_limit lets them back through. check_limit already computes the window boundary internally; this threads that timestamp out so the handler can attach a Retry-After header derived from reset. reset() itself is unchanged, and existing limit semantics are untouched.

224.title: web-frontend: render_checkout uses server totals instead of client-side math
224.body: render_checkout recalculates the order total from line items in the browser, which drifts from the server figure whenever a promo or store credit applies. Support has fielded several 'the total changed at the last step' reports, which is a lousy last impression at checkout. This passes the server-computed total into render_checkout and renders that directly; line items still come from the same payload.

225.title: postgres-ledger: deletion protection for the primary instance
225.body: postgres_ledger.tf has no deletion_protection set and no lifecycle guard, so a stray apply with the wrong workspace could take out the ledger's primary instance. This enables deletion_protection and adds a prevent_destroy lifecycle block on that resource. Restores and normal applies behave exactly as before; only destructive deletes through Terraform are blocked.

226.title: payments-api: typed CaptureResult/RefundResult from capture and refund
226.body: PaymentsService.capture and PaymentsService.refund hand back whatever the provider returns — raw dicts whose shape varies by provider, so every handler digs around for status and amount fields and a renamed key fails quietly. This wraps both paths in small result types (CaptureResult, RefundResult) exposing the fields we actually use, constructed inside the service methods. Provider quirks now stay in one place instead of leaking into handlers.

227.title: refunds: order context in start_refund logs and audit event
227.body: start_refund logs only the workflow id, so when support asks what happened to a given refund we spend the afternoon grepping to tie it back to an order. The opening log line and the audit event now carry order_id, amount, and the requested reason. Small change, but it removes the most tedious step from every refund investigation.

228.title: postgres-ledger: slow query log export in postgres_ledger.tf
228.body: Slow queries on the ledger were only visible by logging into the instance and reading logs by hand, which nobody does until something is already on fire. This enables slow query log capture in postgres_ledger.tf with a one-second threshold and ships the output to our central log pipeline under a dedicated stream. No other instance settings are touched.

229.title: payment-router: structured log of provider choice in route()
229.body: route() picks a provider and hands off, but none of that decision reaches the logs — when a payment lands somewhere unexpected we can only guess why. This adds a single structured log line in route() with the chosen provider, elapsed milliseconds, and the reason it was selected, with a logger wired up in PaymentRouter.__init__. Pure observability change; routing behavior is identical.

158.title: api-gateway: strip trailing slashes in dispatch
158.body: dispatch does an exact string match against the route table, so /cart resolves fine but /cart/ falls through to the 404 handler. This normalizes the incoming path (keeping the root as '/') before the lookup. No changes to any registered route. Testing: added cases in test_routes.py covering /orders/ and /.

159.title: identity-api: fix UTC expiry comparison in verify_refresh_token
159.body: verify_refresh_token compares token expiry against naive datetime.now(), while issue_refresh_token stamps expiry in UTC. On any host set to a non-UTC timezone, perfectly valid tokens fail validation around midnight local time. Both paths now use datetime.now(timezone.utc). I also left a comment on IdentityService documenting the UTC convention so this doesn't drift again. Testing: added a unit test pinning expiry exactly at UTC midnight.

160.title: postgres-ledger: deletion protection and backup retention in postgres_ledger.tf
160.body: Sets deletion_protection = true and backup_retention_days = 14 on the ledger instance, and pins auto_minor_version_upgrade explicitly instead of inheriting the default. The ledger is append-only and we have no restore runbook for it today, so the retention window is the part that matters here. No engine or version changes. Full terraform plan is attached to this PR.

161.title: postgres-main: maintenance window and storage autoscaling in postgres_main.tf
161.body: Adds an explicit maintenance_window (Sunday 04:00-05:00 UTC) and max_allocated_storage so the main instance stops failing nightly bulk loads when it runs out of disk. Also adds a service tag so alert routing picks the instance up correctly. Nothing else touched.

162.title: inventory: raise OutOfStock with SKU detail from reserve
162.body: reserve currently returns None when stock is insufficient, so every caller re-derives the error by hand and the messages drift. This makes reserve raise OutOfStock carrying the SKU and remaining quantity, and registers a handler in app.py that maps it to a 409 with a JSON body. InventoryService behavior is otherwise unchanged. Testing: unit tests for the empty and partial-stock paths.

163.title: cart: extract CartStore from CartService into store.py
163.body: CartService currently owns both orchestration and persistence, which makes the handlers in app.py awkward to test in isolation. This moves the storage half into a new CartStore in store.py: CartService.new_cart and get_cart now delegate to it, and Cart.add / Cart.clear are unchanged. Follow-up will wire an in-memory CartStore for the test suite.

164.title: cart: add hit/miss metrics to CartService.get_cart
164.body: Adds a counter around CartService.get_cart tagged on hit versus miss, plus a debug log in CartStore when Cart.clear wipes a non-empty cart. This came out of trying to explain empty-looking carts in support tickets — right now we have no visibility past the handler. No change to Cart or the public service methods.

165.title: payments-api: structured logging for refund and store helpers
165.body: refund currently emits a single unstructured line, which made last week's support escalation slow to untangle. This adds structured fields (refund_id, order_id) to refund and debug logging in the store helpers: seen/get log hits, store logs the record count, and clear logs when it empties the table. make_key and the refund logic itself are untouched. Testing: added a test asserting clear() leaves the store empty.

238.title: identity-api: reject rotated token families in verify_refresh_token
238.body: verify_refresh_token was still accepting refresh tokens from a family that had already been rotated, so a token stayed usable after the user logged in again. issue_refresh_token now records the family id and generation on each token, and verify_refresh_token compares against the current generation before issuing a new one. Mismatched tokens get a 401 and a warn-level log with the family id so reuse attempts are traceable.

239.title: ledger: validate entries before write in LedgerService.post_entry
239.body:
Malformed payloads were reaching post_entry and surfacing as 500s because LedgerService only checked account existence after opening the write transaction. This moves validation up front: post_entry now rejects negative amounts, mismatched currencies, and unbalanced debit/credit legs with typed error codes before anything is persisted. LedgerService also emits a counter per rejection reason so we can see what clients are actually sending.

Testing: Unit tests cover each rejection path plus one happy-path write against the test database.

240.title: search: skip unchanged docs in build_index via content hashing
240.body: Rebuilding the index re-tokenized every document even when nothing changed, which made build_index take way longer than it needed to on the catalog corpus. It now hashes each document body and skips docs whose hash matches the last run; search behavior is untouched. The first run pays the hashing cost, after that nightly rebuilds should drop most of their runtime.

241.title: identity-api: add audit logging to IdentityService token flows
241.body:
Debugging login-related support tickets was painful because issue_refresh_token and verify_refresh_token had no observability — we couldn't tell whether a failure was an expired token, a rotated family, or an unknown subject. IdentityService now logs subject, client id, and outcome at info level for successes and warn for failures, with a request id threaded through from the handler. Fields are keyed so they can be joined against auth-service events.

Testing: Added tests asserting the log fields for the success case and each failure branch.

242.title: catalog: filter soft-deleted rows in get_product and list_products
242.body:
Product rows are soft-deleted via deleted_at, but get_product and list_products never checked the column, so removed products kept showing in listings until the next full reindex. Both queries now exclude deleted rows, and list_products applies the same filter before paginating. No schema change needed — the index on deleted_at was already in place.

Testing: Regression tests for get_product/list_products against a fixture containing a deleted row.

243.title: auth: unify password and OAuth login through AuthService.login
243.body: The login route in app.py had drifted from AuthService.login — it skipped the rate-limit check and returned a different error shape for bad credentials. The route now just delegates to AuthService.login, and the OAuth path in oauth.py reuses the same session-cookie helper so both flows set cookies identically. Password and OAuth logins now produce consistent error responses.

244.title: ledger: structured logging for post_entry handler failures
244.body:
The post_entry handler in services/ledger/handlers/post_entry.py swallowed parse errors and only logged a generic message, which made bad events nearly impossible to diagnose. Failures now log topic, partition, offset, and a short payload summary at error level, with a metric counting failures by reason. Successful posts are unchanged — this is observability only, no change to how entries are posted.

Testing: Added a test that a malformed event produces the error-level fields and writes nothing to the ledger.

245.title: identity-api: return TokenPair dataclass from issue_refresh_token
245.body: issue_refresh_token and verify_refresh_token returned loose dicts, and after the rotation change in tokens.py the field names ('token' vs 'refresh_token') were easy to mix up — app.py had one such mismatch. Both now return a TokenPair dataclass with access_token, refresh_token, and explicit expiry fields, and callers in IdentityService use attribute access. No wire-format change; response serialization is identical.

198.title: web-frontend: fix stale totals in render_checkout after promo apply
198.body:
render_checkout was rendering the cart snapshot captured at page load, so applying a promo code showed the old total until refresh. It now re-pulls the cart when the promo handler resolves and renders the discount line from the same source. Also routed the page through WebFrontend in app.py so checkout errors get the standard error template instead of a bare traceback.
Testing: Ran checkout locally with a 10% code; total updates without a reload.

199.title: checkout: publish order.placed event from place_order
199.body:
place_order currently commits the order and returns, leaving email and analytics to poll the orders table. This publishes order.placed to the orders topic after the transaction commits, keyed by order id so per-order consumers see events in order. A failed publish is logged loudly but doesn't roll back the committed order; reconciliation picks it up on the next sweep.
Testing: Integration test asserts the event lands on the test topic with the committed order id.

200.title: auth: align login error responses in app.py and oauth.py
200.body: The password login in app.py and the OAuth login in oauth.py return different error shapes — one sends {"error": ...}, the other {"message": ...}, with 400 and 401 used inconsistently. Both paths now funnel through a single formatter on AuthService, so the frontend can render one banner instead of two. Bad credentials are 401 from either flow, malformed requests 400. No change for successful logins.

201.title: cart: get_cart creates guest carts via new_cart instead of 404
201.body: CartService.get_cart 404s for guests with no cart, and the frontend papers over it by catching the error and calling new_cart itself. Moved that into the service: get_cart now creates the cart via new_cart when none exists for the session. One code path instead of two, and the frontend workaround can go away in the next web release.

202.title: postgres-payments: codify deletion protection and backup settings in postgres_payments.tf
202.body: A few settings on this instance only existed in the console: deletion_protection, backup retention, and the maintenance window. This codifies them in postgres_payments.tf so a fresh apply reproduces what's actually running, and adds the service tags the rest of our Terraform modules carry. Also enabled auto_minor_version_upgrade since patching has been a manual step each cycle.

203.title: refunds: reject over-balance amounts in start_refund
203.body:
RefundsService.start_refund happily accepted any positive amount, which meant an over-eager operator (me, last Tuesday) could refund more than the order total and we'd only catch it in reconciliation. start_refund now checks the requested amount against the refundable balance on the order and raises RefundExceedsBalance before anything is queued. The error carries the remaining balance so the response is actually actionable.
Testing: Unit tests cover full, partial, and over-balance amounts.

204.title: checkout: add structured logging and metrics to with_retry
204.body: with_retry logged a single line when it gave up and nothing in between, which made staging incidents hard to reconstruct. Each attempt now emits a structured log with the wrapped function name, attempt number, and error class, plus a checkout_retry_attempts counter labeled by outcome. Everything flows through the existing JSON log handler, so no logging config changes needed.

205.title: checkout: add fresh_state fixture and rewrite place_order tests
205.body:
test_place_order.py was sharing state through a module-level cart, so outcomes depended on test execution order. Added a fresh_state fixture that builds an isolated cart and stubs per test, and rewrote test_place_order_happy_path, test_place_order_empty_cart_fails, and test_place_order_confirmation_mentions_order on top of it. with_retry is stubbed throughout so these assert place_order's logic rather than the wrapper's.
Testing: pytest services/checkout/tests/test_place_order.py passes; full checkout suite green locally.

286.title: web-frontend: make render_checkout rebuild cart context per request
286.body: render_checkout was pulling the cart summary from a module-level cache, so the checkout page kept showing stale line items after a customer edited their cart in another tab. This moves the cache read out of render_checkout and instead passes the summary in as a parameter; the route in app.py now builds that context fresh on each request against the WebFrontend instance. No template changes needed. Testing: added a case in test_checkout_page.py covering the edit-then-navigate flow; existing page tests pass.

287.title: kafka: add order-events topic and explicit retention in kafka.tf
287.body: Adds the order-events topic (24 partitions, rf=3) that the pricing consumer asked for, and sets explicit retention.ms on the checkout topics instead of leaning on broker defaults. Also bumps min.insync.replicas to 2 on the producer-facing topics. Plan output looked clean, no state drift on existing resources. Will apply during Tuesday's maintenance window.

289.title: pricing: reject mixed currencies in PricingService.total_for
289.body: total_for currently sums line totals without checking the currency on each item, so a cart with a stale USD quote next to EUR items produced a nonsense total instead of an error. PricingService now compares each item's currency against the cart currency inside total_for and raises CurrencyMismatch, which app.py maps to a 422 for API callers. The frontend already handles that status from the quote endpoint. Testing: unit tests for the mixed-currency raise and the happy path; full pricing suite green locally.

290.title: api-gateway: return structured 503s from dispatch on upstream timeouts
290.body: dispatch was letting socket timeouts bubble up as bare 500s, which made the dashboards nearly useless during the pricing blip last week. routes.py now catches the timeout inside dispatch, returns a 503 with the upstream service name in the body, and logs elapsed time at warning level. Response shape matches what the web-frontend already parses, so no coordinated release needed.

291.title: checkout: add typed CaptureResult and structured logging to capture_payment
291.body: capture_payment had grown a few implicit contracts — amount could arrive as float or Decimal depending on the caller, and the only failure signal was a bare except that swallowed the message. This pins the signature to Decimal, returns a small CaptureResult dataclass instead of a raw dict, and logs the payment intent status at info with the checkout id attached. No behavior change on the happy path. Testing: existing payments client tests pass unchanged; added one for the malformed-amount branch.

292.title: pricing: round once in total_for after discounting line_total
292.body: line_total rounded each line to two decimals before the percentage discount was applied, so a 15%-off cart could land a cent off depending on item count. discounts.py now applies percentages to the unrounded line value, and total_for rounds a single time at the end; PricingService exposes the same behavior to app.py with no caller changes. Ledger totals and quote totals now agree on all the seeded carts. Testing: property tests on line_total rounding plus the cart fixtures from the finance sheet.

293.title: stripe-adapter: config-driven StripeClient.__init__ and DeclinedError in charge
293.body: StripeClient.__init__ read the API key straight from the environment with no validation, so a missing key surfaced as a confusing AttributeError deep inside charge. The constructor now takes key and timeout explicitly with a clear startup error if config is unset, and charge maps the SDK's card-error responses to our own DeclinedError instead of leaking SDK exception types to callers.

294.title: auth: route both login flows through AuthService.login
294.body: app.py had its own inline login handling for password grants that had drifted from the OAuth path in oauth.py — session length and audit logging differed between the two. This moves both behind AuthService.login, with oauth.py translating the provider callback into the same arguments, so audit events now fire identically for either flow. No changes to token format or cookie names. Testing: extended the auth integration tests to cover login via both the password and provider paths.

337.title: payments-api: rework query-helper tests around the shared work fixture
337.body: The query helper tests were each building their own state inline, which made failures hard to read. This moves them onto the shared `work` fixture and trims the duplicated setup. `test_run_query_returns_rows` now asserts on the rows actually returned instead of just the shape, and the limits test asserts on emitted metrics rather than wall-clock timing, which was flaky on CI.

338.title: catalog: get_product returns None for unknown SKUs; sort param for list_products
338.body: Small QoL change: `CatalogService.get_product` used to raise KeyError for SKUs that were unpublished or mistyped, so every stale link from old marketing emails showed up as a 500 and paged someone. It now returns None and the handler turns that into a clean 404. While in there, `list_products` accepts a `sort` param (name, price, newest) since the storefront folks have asked for it twice.

339.title: refunds: validate amounts in start_refund against order total
339.body: `start_refund` currently accepts any positive amount and only fails later when the ledger rejects it, which leaves half-built refund records behind. This validates the requested amount against the order's paid total up front and raises RefundExceedsOrder with the order id in the message. Also emits a refund.started log line with order_id, amount, and actor so finance's reconciliation dashboard has something stable to key on.

340.title: payment-router: load PaymentRouter rules from config via __init__
340.body: `PaymentRouter` had the provider rules hardcoded inside `route()` as an if-chain, so every new region meant a code change and a deploy. `__init__` now takes a routing table (loaded from config in app.py) mapping predicates to providers, and `route()` walks it in order. When nothing matches we fall back to the default provider and log the unmatched attributes at warn level so coverage gaps are visible.

341.title: payments-api: typed Settings with fail-fast validation in config.py
341.body: config.py had drifted into a grab-bag of os.getenv calls with silent string defaults, so a typo'd variable name only surfaced at runtime as weird behavior. This introduces a Settings dataclass that parses and validates everything at startup — timeouts as ints, feature lists as comma-separated splits — and raises a single error listing every missing or malformed variable. Callers now read attributes off Settings instead of re-parsing env vars ad hoc.

342.title: checkout: validate before reserving in place_order
342.body: `place_order` used to reserve inventory before validating the shipping address, so a bad address burned a reservation and returned a generic 400 after doing real work. Reordered it: cart contents, address, and delivery option are validated first, each failure returning its own error code; inventory reservation happens last, right before the order is persisted. Also added an orders_placed counter tagged by delivery type so we can watch the mix.

343.title: email-sender: raise EmailSendError from send_email; add clear()
343.body: `send_email` was letting raw smtplib exceptions bubble up, which meant the API returned 500s with SMTP internals in the body — fun for nobody. `EmailSenderService.send_email` now wraps failures in EmailSendError carrying the SMTP code, and app.py maps that to a 502 with a stable error payload. Also added `clear()` to reset the in-memory outbox between tests, because monkeypatching module globals on a Friday afternoon was getting old.

344.title: feature-flags: default value for is_enabled, audit logging in set_flag
344.body: Two things bugged me about `FeatureFlagService`. `is_enabled` blew up on flags that didn't exist yet, which made shipping a new flag a two-step dance (deploy code, then create the flag) — it now takes a default and treats unknown flags as that value. And `set_flag` was completely silent; it now logs the previous value, the new one, and the actor, so when someone asks "who turned this off?" we can actually answer.

321.title: web-frontend: await fresh totals in render_checkout before rendering
321.body:
render_checkout was reading the cached cart snapshot before the totals recalculation finished, so a handful of users saw the pre-discount price on the final step. WebFrontend now waits for the fresh totals event before rendering, and logs a warning when it detects a stale snapshot so we can measure how often this actually happens. Checkout markup is untouched.

Testing: added a discounted-cart case to test_checkout_render.py; existing snapshot tests pass.

322.title: api-gateway: include bucket reset time in RateLimited responses from dispatch
322.body: When RateLimited was raised, dispatch returned a bare 429 with no body, which clients couldn't distinguish from a gateway fault. RateLimited now carries the bucket's reset time, and dispatch serializes it into a JSON error envelope with a code clients can key on. check_limit is untouched, and reset still only runs on successful token consumption. Gated behind ratelimit.enriched_errors so we can enable it per-route.

323.title: payments-api: structured logging and typed RefundResult in refund
323.body:
refund used to collapse every processor failure into a generic RefundError, which made support tickets painful to triage. The handler now logs the processor's error code and elapsed time per call, and increments a refund_outcome counter labeled by status. refund also returns a typed RefundResult instead of a loose dict, so callers in checkout can't miss the failure field.

Testing: extended handlers/test_refund.py with declined and timeout cases; type assertions throughout.

324.title: identity-api: tz-aware UTC expiry comparison in verify_refresh_token
324.body:
verify_refresh_token compared expiry against a naive local timestamp, so tokens issued near midnight UTC could fail verification depending on the host clock. issue_refresh_token was already writing UTC; this fixes the read side and pulls a shared utc_now() into tokens.py so both functions use the same clock. Existing tokens verify unchanged — no format or signing changes.

Testing: boundary case added to test_tokens.py pinning the 23:59:59/00:00:00 UTC window.

325.title: identity-api: expired-vs-unknown token metrics in IdentityService
325.body: verify_refresh_token now reports expired versus unknown in the IdentityService rejection metrics, while the public response stays a generic 401 so we don't leak which tokens exist. That split gives us a signal for tuning refresh-token TTLs — right now we're flying blind on whether expirations are user logouts or stale clients. issue_refresh_token gained a debug-level log of the issued TTL for correlating auth spikes with token lifetime.

326.title: redis-cache: allkeys-lru eviction and snapshots off in values.yaml
326.body: This box is a pure cache, so values.yaml now sets maxmemory-policy: allkeys-lru and maxmemory: 2gb — under noeviction, writes started failing outright once we hit the old ceiling. RDB snapshots are off too; nothing here needs to survive a restart, and the fork spikes were showing up in the latency graphs. Plain helm upgrade, no migration. Eviction counts on the dashboard are the thing to watch during rollout.

327.title: pricing: sum in Decimal and round once in total_for
327.body:
total_for rounded each line item to cents before summing, so baskets with many discounted lines drifted a cent or two from what the cart service computed — annoying at checkout, worse in the settlement exports. PricingService now accumulates in Decimal and rounds a single time at the end, which matches the cart's arithmetic exactly. The per-line rounding helper stays for the receipt template, where each row still displays a rounded value.

Testing: property test in test_total_for.py generates randomized baskets and asserts exact equality with cart totals; passing.

328.title: payment-router: hot-reload route table via clear() in PaymentRouter
328.body:
PaymentRouter built its route table once in __init__, so every processor weight change meant a full restart. routing.py now exposes clear(), and app.py calls it when the config watch fires, letting route() pick up new weights within a second of a push. The weighted pick and fallback order inside route() are unchanged.

Testing: added a reload test that rewrites the config file mid-run and asserts the route() distribution shifts; also verified in staging with a canary weight.

353.title: payment-router: replace if/elif in PaymentRouter.route with a table built in __init__
353.body: The if/elif chain in `route` had grown to the point where branch ordering was load-bearing and nobody could explain why. This builds a routing table once in `PaymentRouter.__init__`, keyed on (method, currency), with an explicit fallback entry that preserves today's default-provider behavior. `route` is now a lookup plus a log line recording which provider won and which key matched, so weird routings are at least traceable after the fact. No intended behavior change.

354.title: pricing: compute line_total with Decimal and round only in total_for
354.body: Percent-off discounts were applied as floats in `line_total`, so the same line could price differently depending on how it was itemized, and `total_for` occasionally disagreed with the sum of its own lines by a cent. This switches the arithmetic to Decimal and removes per-line rounding — `total_for` is now the single place that quantizes to cents. Existing stored quotes are unaffected until recalculated.

355.title: fraud-check: gate is_fraudulent on _fresh so a stale model can't auto-flag orders
355.body: `score_order` kept returning the last-computed score when `_fresh` reported the weights were stale, and `is_fraudulent` compared that score against the threshold as if nothing was wrong — a stale model could quietly flag a run of good orders. Now `is_fraudulent` returns False with a `fraud_model_stale` counter when `_fresh` is False, and `score_order` logs the weight age next to the score so staleness is visible in the trace. Scoring with a current model is untouched.

356.title: identity-api: return one generic error from verify_refresh_token
356.body: `verify_refresh_token` distinguished unknown, revoked, and expired tokens in the client-facing error, which made tokens issued by `issue_refresh_token` trivially probeable. Both paths now raise the same `InvalidTokenError` with an identical response body; the specific reason still goes to the server log tagged with the token family, so support can debug without the client learning which case hit. TTL handling in `issue_refresh_token` is unchanged.

357.title: redis-cache: enable TLS in redis_cache.tf and matching helm values
357.body: App clients have been running `rediss://` behind a flag for a while; this turns the server side on. `redis_cache.tf` enables in-transit encryption and an auth token on the cache resource, and `values.yaml` gets the matching `tls.enabled` plus an existing-secret reference so the chart stops holding plaintext. Rollout is two steps — terraform apply, then a helm upgrade per environment — since the managed instance and the chart negotiate independently. Memory and eviction settings untouched.

358.title: postgres-main: add slow-query logging and storage/lag alarms to postgres_main.tf
358.body: Two gaps from poking around after a slow morning: the parameter group now sets `log_min_duration_statement = 200` and `log_statement_stats`, so p95 outliers actually show up in the logs dashboard instead of living in anecdote, and `postgres_main.tf` adds alarms for remaining storage and replica lag that page on-call rather than whoever happens to notice first. Instance class, backup window, and `apply_immediately = false` all unchanged, so this lands with the next maintenance window.

359.title: inventory: raise OutOfStock with sku and availability from every short path in reserve
359.body: Roughly half the shortfall branches in `reserve` raised a bare `ValueError` and half raised `OutOfStock`, so checkout's error mapping worked about half the time and the rest surfaced as a 500. This makes `OutOfStock` the single signal — it now carries `sku`, `requested`, and `available` — and every branch in `reserve` raises it, including the multi-warehouse loop that was silently skipping short locations. Checkout already maps this exception; no caller changes needed.

360.title: checkout: type capture_payment's result and log decline reasons
360.body: `capture_payment` handed callers an untyped dict, and each consumer picked its own keys out of it — two call sites read `decline_code` where the client actually sets `reason`, and quietly got `None`. This introduces a `CaptureResult` dataclass (`approved`, `amount`, `reason`) returned from `capture_payment`, fixes the two call sites reading the wrong key, and adds a debug log with the reason code on declines so support can grep orders without opening the payments dashboard. Caller behavior is otherwise unchanged.

369.title: refunds: validate amount and reason in start_refund
369.body:
start_refund currently accepts any amount and quietly writes a zero-value refund if the caller passes 0 or a negative number. This adds an early check that raises a ValueError including the order id in the message, and requires a non-empty reason string so the ledger trail is actually useful. Also added a debug log at the entry point with order id and amount so a refund can be traced end to end without grepping.

Testing: pytest services/refunds/tests/test_workflow.py, plus three new cases covering zero, negative, and missing reason.

370.title: ledger: add entry_type to LedgerEntry and make FakeBus record publishes
370.body: Two small changes in models.py. LedgerEntry gets an entry_type field (debit/credit/adjustment) defaulting to 'debit' so existing constructors keep working; this lets the nightly reconciliation job filter adjustments without string-matching on the memo field. FakeBus.publish now appends (topic, payload) tuples to a public .sent list, so tests can assert on the exact publish order instead of patching the bus. Nothing downstream changes since entry_type is additive and FakeBus is test-only.

371.title: postgres-payments: enable deletion protection and extend backup retention
371.body: This turns on deletion_protection for the payments cluster and bumps the automated backup retention window from 7 to 14 days. It also pins a fixed maintenance window (Sunday 04:00 UTC) so minor version upgrades stop landing mid-morning. Storage encryption was already in place via the existing KMS key; nothing else in the module is touched.

372.title: web-frontend: fix penny rounding in render_checkout order summary
372.body:
render_checkout was summing line totals as floats, so the order summary occasionally showed 19.999999... instead of 20.00 and the displayed total didn't match what the ledger recorded. It now converts each line to Decimal at the boundary and formats with quantize, and WebFrontend passes the currency code through so the template stops hardcoding '$'. Sessions without a currency still render since it defaults to USD.

Testing: pytest services/web_frontend/tests, including a three-line cart that reproduces the rounding bug.

373.title: search: add category and price filters to SearchService.search and index them in build_index
373.body:
build_index now writes category and price_range fields alongside the existing product text so filtering happens at the index level instead of after the fact in app.py. SearchService.search accepts optional category and max_price kwargs, both translated into index-level clauses. This came out of the storefront wanting 'under $50 in kitchen' style queries without a second round-trip through the catalog service. The rebuild is backward compatible; existing shards ignore the new fields until reindexed.

Testing: pytest for the filter clauses, plus a manual diff of top-20 results for the fifty most common queries before/after.

374.title: redis-cache: switch eviction to allkeys-lru and enable TLS in transit
374.body: values.yaml now sets maxmemory-policy to allkeys-lru; the old volatile-lru setting silently no-ops now that catalog keys are written without expiries, so under memory pressure Redis was returning errors instead of evicting. On the terraform side, the cache resource gets tls enabled plus an auth token. No app code changes needed since the clients already speak TLS.

375.title: postgres-payments: add disk and CPU CloudWatch alarms
375.body: Adds two CloudWatch alarms on the payments cluster: one at 80% disk and one at 85% CPU sustained for 15 minutes, both routing to the infra-alerts SNS topic. This replaces the habit of manually checking the console on Monday mornings. Also adds the standard service and environment tags so the alarm dashboards group correctly.

376.title: kafka: raise orders topic retention to 72h and enable per-topic monitoring
376.body:
Bumps the cluster to Kafka 3.6 (rolling, broker-by-broker) and raises retention.ms on the orders topic from 24h to 72h, so a consumer that's offline for a weekend can catch up from the log rather than doing a full reload from the source tables. Also flips monitoring to PER_TOPIC_PER_BROKER so lag shows up per topic in Grafana instead of as one cluster-wide number.

Testing: terraform plan reviewed and applied to staging first; consumer lag stayed flat during the rolling upgrade and no rebalance alerts fired.

313.title: postgres-ledger: parameterize postgres_ledger.tf and enable deletion protection
313.body:
The ledger database config was fully hardcoded in infra/terraform/postgres_ledger.tf, which made staging drift a recurring nuisance. This moves the instance class, backup retention, and maintenance window into variables with defaults matching prod, and enables deletion_protection on the production module. Adds the standard service/owner tags while I'm in there so the inventory report stops flagging it as unowned.

Testing: terraform plan against staging shows only the expected tag and deletion_protection diffs; prod apply after review.

314.title: api-gateway: return 405 with Allow header from dispatch
314.body:
dispatch() in services/api_gateway/routes.py was collapsing method mismatches into a plain 404, which made client-side debugging harder than it needed to be. Route matching now keeps the path match around and, when the path exists under a different verb, responds 405 with an Allow header listing the supported methods. Unmatched paths still 404 exactly as before.

Testing: new table cases in tests/test_routes.py cover the 404/405 split and the Allow header contents.

315.title: auth: enforce state validation in oauth.login
315.body: oauth.py was completing provider callbacks without checking the state parameter, so a crafted redirect could finish a login that someone else started. login() now compares state against the signed cookie set at flow start and bails with a 400 on mismatch. AuthService grew a small verify_state helper so the login route in app.py stays thin. Happy path is untouched; poked at the mismatch path against the staging provider by hand.

316.title: payment-router: replace route() conditionals with a processor registry
316.body:
PaymentRouter.route() had turned into a chain of hardcoded conditionals, so wiring up a new processor meant editing the hot path and hoping nothing else shifted. __init__ now builds a processor registry from config, and route() does a single lookup with a fallback to the default processor when a key is missing. Selections are logged with processor name and region so routing decisions are traceable from request logs.

Testing: unit tests cover registry construction and the fallback branch; a staging run shows identical processor choices to main.

317.title: feature-flags: add short-TTL cache to FeatureFlagService.is_enabled
317.body: Every is_enabled() call in services/feature_flags/app.py went straight to Redis, which is fine until a page render fans out a few dozen flag checks at once. FeatureFlagService now keeps a small in-process cache with a 5-second TTL, and set_flag bumps a version key so stale entries get skipped on the next read. Worst case, a flag change takes about five seconds to reach a given instance, which is acceptable for everything we flag today.

318.title: identity-api: rotate refresh tokens on exchange in tokens.py
318.body: verify_refresh_token() currently hands back the same token until it expires, so a token copied off a shared machine keeps working long after it should have. tokens.py now issues a fresh refresh token on every exchange and marks the presented one consumed in the same transaction; verify_refresh_token rejects anything already consumed. Callers already read the refreshed-token field from the response, so no client change is needed.

319.title: ledger: reject unbalanced batches in post_entry
319.body:
post_entry() in services/ledger/handlers/post_entry.py currently accepts batches where debits and credits don't sum to zero, and the imbalance only surfaces hours later in a reconciliation query. The handler now checks balance before writing anything and returns a structured rejection naming the offending lines, plus a reject counter for dashboards. On failure, nothing partial lands in the journal.

Testing: randomized unbalanced batches in tests/ledger/test_post_entry.py all come back as clean rejections.

320.title: checkout: add typing and completion logging to with_retry
320.body: with_retry() in services/checkout/retry.py was an untyped decorator, so mypy had been shrugging at every call site that passed keyword arguments through. This adds ParamSpec/TypeVar annotations plus one structured log line on completion carrying the wrapped function name, attempts used, and final outcome — until now the per-attempt debug logs were the only visibility we had. The loop itself is untouched.

361.title: postgres-payments: slow-query logging and CloudWatch log export in postgres_payments.tf
361.body: The payments cluster has been a black box whenever order latency spikes. This adds an aws_db_parameter_group with track_io_timing on and log_min_duration_statement set to 250ms in postgres_payments.tf, and ships the Postgres logs to CloudWatch so we can query them instead of grepping instance logs. Parameters apply at the next maintenance window; nothing else about the cluster changes.

362.title: cart: return None from CartService.get_cart for expired carts
362.body: CartService.get_cart was raising when it hit a cart row already cleaned up by the nightly expiry job, which customers saw as a 500 on the basket page. It now returns None like the not-found path does, and logs a warning with the cart id so we can spot if expiry is running ahead of the cookie TTL. While I was in there, new_cart stamps created_at explicitly instead of leaning on the DB default, which makes the expiry job's cutoff math easier to reason about.

363.title: fraud-check: add score_order metrics and structured flagged-decision logs
363.body: Right now the only way to see what FraudService is doing is grep the app logs. This adds a statsd histogram on score_order (score and latency, tagged by rule version) and a structured log line in is_fraudulent whenever an order crosses the fraud threshold, including order id and the top contributing features. The scoring itself is untouched — is_fraudulent returns exactly the same booleans — this just makes decisions observable before we go anywhere near the thresholds.

364.title: postgres-ledger: deletion protection and PITR for the ledger instance in postgres_ledger.tf
364.body: The ledger instance currently has deletion_protection unset and a one-day backup window, which feels thin for the one datastore we can't reconstruct from anywhere else. This sets deletion_protection = true, bumps backup_retention_period to 14 days, and enables point-in-time recovery so we can restore to an arbitrary timestamp if a migration ever goes sideways. Also adding a prevent-destroy lifecycle block in postgres_ledger.tf as a belt-and-braces guard against a stray apply.

365.title: notifications: catch render failures in run_consumer instead of crashing
365.body: run_consumer currently blows up the whole consumer loop whenever render throws on a malformed template context, so one bad order confirmation backs up the queue for everyone behind it. NotificationsService now handles render failures per message, logs the template name and correlation id, and ships the message to the dead-letter topic instead of taking the loop down. Also inlined the plain-text fallback for shipping_notice in templates.py, since we were maintaining two copies of the same copy.

366.title: fraud-check: extract scoring into model.py behind FraudService
366.body: This splits FraudService in two: app.py keeps request handling and the is_fraudulent threshold logic, while feature assembly and score_order move into model.py. The new _fresh() helper checks the model artifact's mtime and reloads it when a retrained version lands, so score_order picks up new weights without a service restart. No behavior change on the current model — I diffed scores across 10k replayed orders and the outputs are bit-identical.

367.title: postgres-payments: storage autoscaling and performance insights in postgres_payments.tf
367.body: We've paged twice this quarter on disk alarms on the payments primary with nothing to do but resize by hand. This sets max_allocated_storage so the gp3 volume grows automatically up to the configured cap, and enables performance insights with a week of retention so the next slow-INSERT incident has actual wait events attached to it. Both are instance-level settings in postgres_payments.tf; the apply does a brief storage modification but no restart.

368.title: web-frontend: empty-cart and inline error handling in render_checkout
368.body: render_checkout assumed the cart always has at least one line, so a trimmed cart or expired session gave customers a blank checkout and a stack trace in our logs. WebFrontend now renders a proper empty-state panel with a link back to the catalog, and field errors from the order call show inline next to the form instead of a generic banner. Also hoisted currency formatting into one helper so totals and per-line amounts can't disagree.

385.title: pricing: round totals once in PricingService.total_for
385.body:
PricingService.total_for was summing line items as floats, so multi-item orders could drift by a cent depending on item order. The accumulator is now Decimal, rounded once at the end instead of per add, which matches what the receipts service expects. Also tightened the type hints on total_for so mypy catches callers passing formatted strings.

Testing: added 3-item and 100-item cart cases to test_pricing.py; both pass.

386.title: feature-flags: add short-TTL cache to FeatureFlagService.is_enabled
386.body: is_enabled was hitting Redis on every check even for flags that hadn't changed, which added noticeable latency to the checkout render path. FeatureFlagService now keeps a small in-process cache with a short TTL, and set_flag publishes an invalidation on the flags channel so peers drop stale entries quickly. Also made is_enabled return False for unknown flags instead of raising — every caller was wrapping it in try/except anyway.

387.title: stripe-adapter: structured logging and metrics in StripeClient.charge
387.body:
charge() was dumping full request/response objects at INFO, which made grepping for one transaction miserable and leaked card metadata into the logs. StripeClient now emits a compact structured event per call (route, outcome, latency) and increments counters we can alert on. __init__ takes the log level explicitly so tests can silence it.

Testing: unit tests cover the redaction path and metric tags; verified against the Stripe sandbox fixtures.

388.title: pricing: extract shared line_total helper for total_for and discounts
388.body: The line-total math lived inline in PricingService.total_for and was duplicated in two places in discounts.py, and the copies had already drifted on how stacked discounts round. This pulls it into a single line_total helper in discounts.py that total_for also calls, so there's exactly one rounding rule. Public signatures in discounts.py are unchanged.

389.title: identity-api: typed failure reasons from verify_refresh_token
389.body: verify_refresh_token collapsed every failure into one generic 'invalid' response, so we couldn't tell an expired token from an unknown one in the logs. issue_refresh_token now stamps a family id and issued-at claim, and verify_refresh_token returns a typed reason (expired, unknown, malformed) that the handler maps to the right status code. No change to the wire format clients see.

390.title: auth: constant-time failure path in oauth.login
390.body:
login returned different errors for a missing account versus a bad password, at slightly different speeds — small leak, but it doesn't need to exist. The failure path is now constant-time, and each failed attempt logs a single warn event with the tenant id, no usernames. Also moved the redirect-uri check ahead of the token exchange so obvious mismatches fail before any network call.

Testing: added cases for unknown account, bad password, and mismatched redirect to test_oauth.py.

391.title: postgres-main: deletion protection and pinned backup window in postgres_main.tf
391.body:
postgres_main.tf had deletion protection off and no explicit backup window, so nightly backups landed whenever the provider felt like it. This pins the window to 03:10–03:40 UTC, enables deletion protection, and adds the standard Northwind tags so the inventory report stops flagging the instance. Also turned on storage autoscaling at 100 GB so a full disk stops paging us.

Testing: terraform plan reviewed and applied in staging first; a destroy plan confirms protection blocks it.

392.title: postgres-main: pg_stat_statements and slow-query logging in postgres_main.tf
392.body: We usually hear about slow queries from a user long before we see them in the database, so this wires pg_stat_statements into the parameter group (shared_preload_libraries plus the track flag) and sets log_min_duration_statement to 500ms. I also set a Sunday-morning maintenance window and bumped log retention to 14 days so we can correlate with the app logs. Nothing structural changed — just observability knobs.

442.title: ledger: reject unbalanced journal entries in LedgerService.post_entry
442.body: `LedgerService.post_entry` currently accepts entries whose debit and credit legs don't sum to zero and only fails when the persistence layer's constraint fires, producing a confusing traceback with no context about the amounts involved. This adds an explicit check in `post_entry` that raises `ValueError` with the entry reference, the debit total, and the credit total before anything is written. The error path also logs a warning so malformed entries from upstream producers show up in the ledger dashboard instead of surfacing as raw tracebacks. Testing: added unit cases for balanced, over-debited, and over-credited entries; all green locally.

443.title: refunds: return the created Refund from start_refund and log the reason
443.body: `start_refund` returns None today, so every caller re-queries the refund by order id immediately after calling it. It now returns the record it just created, and the two call sites in workflow.py were updated to use it directly. I also added the `reason` argument to the audit log line — right now there's no way to tell a support-issued refund from a policy refund after the fact. No other behavior change.

444.title: postgres-main: enable deletion protection and 30-day backups in postgres_main.tf
444.body: Brings `infra/terraform/postgres_main.tf` in line with the tier-1 datastore checklist: `deletion_protection = true`, backup retention window from 7 to 30 days, and the `data-classification: confidential` tag. Also sets `copy_tags_to_snapshot` so the snapshot inventory stays attributable. Plan is clean apart from the in-place parameter applies; apply needs coordinating with whoever is on pager that week.

445.title: api-gateway: map RateLimited to a 429 with Retry-After in dispatch
445.body: When `check_limit` trips, the `RateLimited` exception currently bubbles out of `dispatch` and surfaces as a 500, which makes well-behaved clients look like they hit a server bug. `RateLimited` now carries a `retry_after` field populated from the window's reset time, and `dispatch` catches it and returns a 429 JSON body with the `Retry-After` header set. `reset` is unchanged; the tests needed a clock seam so the window boundary is injectable. Testing: unit tests with a fake clock covering the boundary case and the header value.

446.title: payments-api: validate amount and currency in PaymentsService.capture and .refund
446.body: `capture` and `refund` pass whatever they receive straight to the gateway, so a zero amount or a currency mismatch against the original charge only fails at Stripe with an opaque error code. Both methods now validate up front and raise `InvalidAmount` / `InvalidCurrency` with the offending values. Also added a structured success log with the gateway reference and masked amounts, which support has been reconstructing by hand from raw responses. Testing: unit tests for negative, zero, and mismatched-currency inputs on both methods.

447.title: kafka: disable auto topic creation and add under-replication alarm in kafka.tf
447.body: Two changes to `infra/terraform/kafka.tf`. First, `auto_create_topics_enable` goes off — typo'd producer topics have appeared twice this quarter and silently absorb traffic until someone notices the empty consumer lag; topics must now exist in the topics module. Second, a CloudWatch alarm on `UnderReplicatedPartitions > 0` for 15 minutes, wired to the data-platform Slack notification. Both are broker-config applies, no restarts.

448.title: checkout: return 409 with short SKUs from place_order on stock failure
448.body: `place_order` currently converts `OutOfStockError` into a generic 500, so shoppers see 'something went wrong' and support can't distinguish inventory problems from real bugs. The handler now returns a 409 whose body lists the short SKUs with requested vs available quantities, plus an INFO log line with the cart id. The front end already has a slot for this shape — they've been rendering the fallback path for everyone since last sprint. Testing: handler tests with a mocked inventory client; verified the 409 body against the front end's parser.

449.title: catalog: type-hint and document Product lookups in models.py
449.body: `get_product` returns None for a missing sku while `list_products` quietly drops the same product, and neither is annotated, so callers keep guessing. This adds full type hints (`Optional[Product]` from `get_product`, `Sequence[Product]` from `list_products`) and docstrings spelling out the discontinued-product behavior on each path. No runtime behavior change here — the call-site cleanup in checkout and search can follow once the contract is explicit.

410.title: postgres-ledger: enable deletion protection and pin backup window in postgres_ledger.tf
410.body: Someone set the backup window by hand in the console months ago and terraform has been showing drift on this cluster ever since. This pins maintenance_window and backup_window to the values actually running and enables deletion protection while I'm in the file. If you need the window moved, change the tf and apply — not the console.

411.title: checkout: add reason codes to validation failures in place_order
411.body: When place_order rejects an order we return a bare 400 and the only trace is a one-line log with no context, which turns every support escalation into a guessing game. This adds a structured log line next to the rejection with the cart id, the failing check, and a short reason code (empty_cart, invalid_quantity, unknown_sku). Status codes and response shape are unchanged — this is purely observability.

412.title: checkout: cover empty-cart and confirmation cases in test_place_order.py
412.body: test_place_order_happy_path was the only test in the file, which is the testing equivalent of one smoke detector in a warehouse. This pulls the duplicated setup into a fresh_state fixture and adds two cases: test_place_order_empty_cart_fails checks that place_order rejects an empty cart with the right error, and test_place_order_confirmation_mentions_order asserts the confirmation text includes the order reference. No production changes in this PR.

413.title: ledger: make outbox.relay skip entries it already published
413.body: When a relay batch died partway through publishing, the next pass re-scanned the outbox from the top and pushed the same entries to the bus again, and a few downstream consumers did not enjoy that. relay now tracks the entry_ids it has handled within a pass and skips those rows on re-scan. The new test_relay_dedupes_on_entry_id covers the re-scan case, and test_post_entry_publishes_to_bus confirms the normal save → publish path is untouched.
