The sample_entry/reset helpers in setup_function made both quick to write.

414.title: postgres-ledger: export slow query logs and set statement_timeout in postgres_ledger.tf
414.body: A couple of ad-hoc analytics queries have been running for hours on the ledger cluster and nobody notices until the dashboards look strange. This turns on slow query log export to our existing logging pipeline and sets statement_timeout to 15 minutes in the parameter group, so runaway queries get cut and leave a trace we can actually grep. The timeout applies to the ledger cluster only; payments keeps its own settings.

415.title: kafka: add ledger.entry.v2 topic and raise orders retention in kafka.tf
415.body: Ledger wants a clean topic with an explicit schema config instead of piggybacking on orders.events, so this adds ledger.entry.v2 with its own partition count and schema registry entry. Also bumps orders.events retention from 24h to 72h — the last bad deploy would have been a non-event with that much reprocess headroom. Terraform-only; no broker restarts required.

416.title: cart: stop recomputing totals on every get_cart read
416.body: CartService.get_cart walks every line item and recalculates totals on each read, which was cute when carts had three items and less cute now. The writers on CartService already keep a stored totals column current, so get_cart can just read what's there. Cart reads were our slowest endpoint on the cart page last week; this should flatten that considerably.

417.title: postgres-payments: enable PITR and deletion protection in postgres_payments.tf
417.body: Payments is the one dataset where "restore from last night's snapshot" isn't a real answer, so this enables point-in-time recovery with 14-day retention and switches on deletion protection for the instance. It also staggers the maintenance window to Sunday evening so the ledger and payments clusters aren't bouncing at the same time. No parameter changes in this one.

459.title: notifications: handle missing context keys in templates.render
459.body: render() raised a KeyError whenever a template referenced a variable that wasn't in the context dict, which is how last week's digest batch died halfway through send. Missing keys now render as an empty string and log a warning with the template name and key, so a bad context is visible instead of fatal. Fixed the identical lookup bug in the subject-line path while I was in there.

460.title: fraud-check: cast FraudService.score_order output to plain floats
460.body: FraudService.score_order returns numpy.float64, which json.dumps refuses to serialize, so flagged orders logged a 'TypeError: float64 not JSON serializable' instead of an audit record. The score is now cast to a built-in float and rounded to four decimals before it reaches the response or the audit log. While in there, is_fraudulent logs the numeric score next to the boolean — reviewing flagged orders with just true/false was painful. Testing: unit case for the numpy-to-float conversion plus a json.dumps round-trip; existing suite passes.

461.title: checkout: typed errors from capture_payment, handled in place_order
461.body: capture_payment raised a bare ValueError on every non-2xx from the payments provider, so place_order couldn't tell a customer decline from a malformed request — everything landed in one generic path and orders stuck in 'processing'. This adds CaptureDeclinedError and CaptureError in clients/payments.py; place_order catches the declined case, marks the order payment_declined, and returns a clear message to the client while everything else bubbles to the existing handler. Happy path is unchanged. Testing: new cases in tests/test_place_order.py covering declined vs. malformed responses.

462.title: payment-router: lazy credential load in PaymentRouter.__init__
462.body: PaymentRouter.__init__ fetched provider credentials from the secrets store at construction, so merely importing the app for a smoke test or schema check hit the network. Credentials now load on the first route() call and are cached on the instance; the selection logic in route() itself is unchanged. This also lets handler tests take a stub router without stubbing the secrets client.

463.title: payment-router: atomic table swap in routing.clear
463.body: clear() rebuilt the routing table in place, so a route() call iterating the old dict could raise KeyError mid-lookup during a config reload. The replacement table is now built fully and rebound to the module-level reference in a single assignment — readers see either the old table or the new one. Added a debug log in clear() with the resulting provider count. Testing: test hammers route() from threads while clear() runs; previously flaky, now deterministic.

464.title: checkout: return order_id and placed_at from CheckoutService.place_order
464.body: place_order currently returns only a status flag, so the confirmation page has to guess the order reference or poll the orders list until the new order appears. The response now includes order_id and an ISO-8601 placed_at timestamp. Also added an INFO log at the top of place_order with cart size and total — we currently have zero visibility into where in the flow abandoned checkouts bail out.

465.title: search: accent-insensitive tokens in indexer.build_index
465.body: build_index tokenized as-is, so 'Crème Fraîche Kit' was unfindable by 'creme' and 'Cafe' never matched 'Café'. Tokens are lowercased and stripped of diacritics (unicodedata NFD normalize, drop combining marks) before hitting the index, and hyphenated SKUs like NW-2204 keep both the full token and its parts. search() needed no changes — the improvement is entirely at index time.

466.title: postgres-payments: deletion protection and 14-day backups
466.body: The payments database module shipped with deletion_protection unset and backup_retention_period at 1, thinner than any of our other stateful infra. This sets deletion_protection = true, bumps retention to 14 days, pins an explicit backup_window outside peak traffic, and adds final_snapshot_identifier so a stray destroy still leaves a snapshot. Added the standard service/owner tags for the catalog too. Testing: terraform plan reviewed against staging; applying there first, then prod in the Tuesday window.

426.title: catalog: add discontinued_at to Product and filter it from list_products
426.body:
Discontinued SKUs still show up in storefront listings because list_products ignores lifecycle state. This adds a nullable `discontinued_at` column to Product, excludes rows where it's set from list_products, and backfills from the legacy `active` flag in a migration. get_product still returns discontinued rows so order-history lookups keep working.

Testing: fixtures for active and discontinued rows; verified the backfill against a staging snapshot.

427.title: kafka: pin retention.ms and cleanup policy on orders.events in kafka.tf
427.body: orders.events inherits broker defaults today, so its retention window shifts whenever broker config changes, and the analytics replay job has already lost data to that once. This pins retention.ms at 604800000 and sets cleanup.policy=delete explicitly on the topic, and tags the resource so it shows up in the infra inventory. Terraform plan shows in-place topic config updates only.

428.title: postgres-payments: enable deletion protection and 14-day backups in postgres_payments.tf
428.body:
The payments database currently runs with deletion protection off and a 3-day backup window, which is thinner than our recovery objectives for financial data. This turns on deletion protection, raises backup_retention_period to 14, and sets copy_tags_to_snapshot so snapshots carry the same tags as the cluster. Applying to staging first; production follows after the next maintenance window.

Testing: terraform plan/apply against staging; confirmed a manual destroy attempt is rejected.

429.title: catalog: return None from get_product for unknown SKUs
429.body: get_product raises CatalogError on a missing SKU today, and the API layer turns that into a 500 for what is really a 404. This changes get_product to return None when the row doesn't exist and reserves the exception for corrupt records. Storefront handlers already treat a falsy result as not-found, so nothing else needs to move.

430.title: identity-api: enforce audience claim in verify_refresh_token
430.body:
verify_refresh_token checks signature and expiry but not audience, so a token minted for the mobile client is accepted by the web session flow. issue_refresh_token already stamps an `aud` claim; this adds the corresponding check in verify_refresh_token via IdentityService and rejects mismatches with a dedicated error code. Tokens issued before the claim existed fail the check, but they expire within 24 hours.

Testing: added cases for cross-audience reuse and legacy tokens without `aud`.

431.title: payment-router: replace route() branches with a selection table built in PaymentRouter.__init__
431.body:
route() has grown into a wall of hardcoded branches — every new acquirer means editing match arms across a couple of currency special cases. This builds the provider selection table in PaymentRouter.__init__, keyed by currency and region, and reduces route() to a lookup with a fallback to the default provider. Also logs the chosen provider at debug and increments a route_decision counter so the distribution is visible in dashboards.

Testing: table-driven tests per currency/region pair plus the fallback path.

432.title: api-gateway: structured JSON access logs from dispatch
432.body: dispatch emits a single unstructured log line today, which makes tracing slow cross-service calls miserable. This switches it to structured JSON access logs carrying route, upstream service, status, and latency_ms, and adds upstream latency as a histogram metric. Log volume is unchanged — only the shape — so the current sink and existing alerts keep working as-is.

433.title: postgres-payments: add replica-lag and disk alarms in postgres_payments.tf
433.body: We learned about last week's replica failover from a payments-service error spike rather than an alert. This adds CloudWatch alarms on replica lag (over 5s for 10 minutes) and disk usage above 80%, and exports the postgres slow-query log to the existing log group so it can be correlated with the query metrics we already collect. Thresholds match what the ledger replicas already run.

PLAT-337.title: Add cache hit/miss ratio graphs to the session-cache Grafana dashboard
PLAT-337.description: The session-cache Grafana panel currently only shows memory usage and eviction counts, so checking hit rate means SSHing in and running redis-cli by hand. Export the INFO stats (keyspace_hits/keyspace_misses) via the existing redis-exporter and add hit/miss ratio graphs per cache name to the dashboard. Impact: engineers can spot cache-waste after config changes without manual checks. Acceptance: dashboard shows a 24h hit ratio per cache at 5-minute resolution.

GRW-304.title: Catalog browse filter returns products from archived categories
GRW-304.description: On the catalog browse page, filtering by an archived category still returns products whose only assignment is to that category (repro: filter by 'Seasonal — 2023' in staging). The category filter query doesn't exclude status='archived', and archived categories also still appear in the filter dropdown. Impact: merchandisers see stale products and report them as data bugs. Acceptance: archived categories are excluded from both the filter query and the dropdown, with a unit test covering the case.

GRW-274.title: Downgrade full search request payload logging from INFO to DEBUG
GRW-274.description: SearchService logs the entire request body (query text, sort options, facet lists) at INFO on every request, which makes the CloudWatch log group noisy and hard to grep during incidents. Move the full payload to DEBUG and log a one-line INFO summary instead: query length, result count, and latency. Acceptance: INFO output is a single line per request; the DEBUG payload is still available when tracing a specific query.

GRW-358.title: Fix flaky CatalogImageUploadIT assertion on async thumbnail resize
GRW-358.description: CatalogImageUploadIT fails roughly 1 in 6 CI runs because it asserts on the resized thumbnail immediately after upload, before the async resize job has finished writing it. Change the test to poll for the thumbnail's presence with a timeout (up to 10s) instead of asserting right away. Impact: removes the most common source of red CI builds on the catalog pipeline. Acceptance: the test passes 20 consecutive CI runs.

CHK-50.title: Fix layout shift on checkout summary when a promo code is applied
CHK-50.description: When a shopper applies a valid promo code on the checkout page, the order totals section re-renders about 300ms later and shifts the 'Place Order' button down mid-click. Repro: add any item to the cart, enter code NORTH10, and click Place Order as the totals refresh. Users on slower connections end up misclicking the wrong element. Acceptance: totals update without moving any interactive controls, verified with a visual regression snapshot.

LED-243.title: Include batch ID and rejection reason in ledger journal validation logs
LED-243.description: When a journal batch fails validation, the ledger logs only a generic 'batch rejected' line, so anyone investigating has to trace the batch by hand. Repro: submit a journal batch with a mismatched debit/credit total via the internal tool and inspect the ledger logs. Acceptance: the rejection log entry includes the batch ID, the failing rule name, and the offending line numbers, using the existing structured logging format.

CHK-40.title: Stabilize flaky cart badge count test in the storefront E2E suite
CHK-40.description: The 'cart badge shows correct item count' Cypress test fails intermittently in CI, roughly 1 in 8 runs, because it asserts before the mocked cart API response resolves. Repro: run the storefront E2E suite locally several times or check the nightly CI job history. Acceptance: the test waits deterministically on the mocked cart response and passes 25 consecutive CI runs before we close this.

PLAT-102.title: Return a clearer 413 response body when request payloads exceed the gateway limit
PLAT-102.description: Requests over 1 MB hitting the api-gateway receive a bare 413 with an empty body, so client teams cannot tell whether to trim the payload or escalate. Repro: POST a 2 MB JSON body to any v1 route and inspect the raw response. Impact: integrating teams waste time debugging silent errors. Acceptance: the gateway returns a JSON error naming the route's size limit and linking to the payload guidelines page in the developer docs.

PLAT-274.title: Add audit log entries for flag toggles made via the feature-flags admin UI
PLAT-274.description: When a flag is flipped in the feature-flags admin UI, the change only shows up in eval logs, making it hard to trace who changed what and when. Added an audit log entry capturing the actor, flag key, old/new value, and environment for every UI toggle. Verified in staging against the checkout flag set; entries now appear in the audit stream within a second. Acceptance: every UI toggle produces exactly one audit record with the correct actor and value diff.

GRW-296.title: Fix flaky search suggestions test caused by unsorted ranking ties
GRW-296.description: The suggestions unit test in search fails intermittently when two candidate phrases have identical scores, because output order depends on map iteration. Fixed by breaking ties alphabetically by phrase and updated the fixture to cover the tie case. Repro: run the suggestions suite 10 times locally; it failed roughly 3 of 10 runs before the fix. Acceptance: 20 consecutive green runs in CI.

PLAT-18.title: Return 404 instead of 500 for unknown flag keys in the eval endpoint
PLAT-18.description: Evaluating a non-existent flag key against the feature-flags public eval endpoint returned a 500 with a stack trace instead of a clean 404. Updated the handler to look up the flag first and return 404 with a short error body. Repro: curl the eval endpoint with flagKey=nope and observe the previous response. Acceptance: unknown keys return 404 and log at warn level, not error, keeping error dashboards clean.

PLAT-392.title: Document percentage rollout and rollback steps in the feature-flags README
PLAT-392.description: The README still describes the old two-step rollout process, and recent questions in support channels suggest the current percentage-based rollout is undocumented. Rewrite the rollout section to cover percentage stages, targeting rules, and the rollback shortcut, with one worked example using a fictional flag. Include a short troubleshooting table for common mistakes like targeting the wrong environment or forgetting a segment. Acceptance: README reviewed by one other engineer and linked from the service homepage.

PLAT-333.title: Log per-statement duration for migrations run against postgres-payments
PLAT-333.description: Migrations applied to the postgres-payments database logged only start and finish timestamps, so it was impossible to tell which step was slow. Extended the migration runner to log each statement with its duration at INFO and emit a WARN for anything over two seconds. Repro: run the latest backfill migration in staging and inspect the log output. Acceptance: every statement appears with a duration and slow steps are clearly flagged.

PLAT-99.title: Emit eval-count metric tagged by flag key and environment
PLAT-99.description: The feature-flags service exposes a single aggregate request counter, so we cannot see which flags actually drive traffic. Adding a counter for evaluations tagged with flag_key and environment, with a low-cardinality guard that skips denylisted keys. Wiring it into the eval handler and exporting it to the existing metrics pipeline. Acceptance: metric visible on the staging dashboard within five minutes, letting us spot stale zero-traffic flags before cleanup.

PAY-64.title: Replace full webhook payload logging with structured event lines in the Stripe adapter
PAY-64.description: The Stripe adapter currently logs full webhook payloads at DEBUG, which is noisy and occasionally trips the log-size limit on large events. Replacing these with a structured line containing event type, payload size, and outcome, keeping full payloads behind a temporary debug flag. Repro: send a test invoice event from the Stripe sandbox and inspect the adapter logs. Acceptance: no full payloads in default logs and a structured line present for every webhook.

CHK-182.title: Fix misaligned totals row on the checkout summary panel
CHK-182.description: On the checkout summary panel, the order-total row shifts a few pixels left whenever a discount label is present, because the label and amount share a flex row with inconsistent padding. Repro: add a percentage discount to a cart and compare the totals row against a cart without one. Fixed by aligning amounts to a fixed-width column and added a snapshot test covering the discounted state. Acceptance: totals align identically with and without a discount label.

IDN-209.title: Return field-level validation errors for malformed emails in identity-api
IDN-209.description: The identity-api signup endpoint rejects malformed emails with a generic 'invalid input' message, generating repeated support questions. Added field-level validation that returns the offending field and a short reason, such as 'email: missing @-sign', and documented the accepted format in the API reference. Repro: POST a signup with the email hana.example. Acceptance: the response body names the field and reason, and the docs include format examples.

PLAT-152.title: Add consumer-lag dashboard panels for missing event bus topics
PLAT-152.description: The shared Kafka consumer-lag dashboard covers only a handful of topics, and several newer event bus topics have no panel at all. Adding per-topic lag panels for all registered northwind event bus topics with sensible thresholds and a link from the service runbook. Repro: compare the dashboard topic list against the topic registry; multiple topics are missing. Acceptance: every registered topic has a lag panel and the runbook links to the dashboard.

IDN-336.title: Expired sessions show 'Something went wrong' instead of redirecting to login
IDN-336.description: Repro: leave the dashboard idle for 30 minutes, then click any link — the app renders a bare 'Something went wrong' error instead of the login screen. Users assume the site is broken and file support tickets rather than signing in again. Expired sessions should redirect to /login with a 'Your session has expired' banner. Acceptance: an idle timeout lands on the login page with the banner, and no 500 is logged for the expired-session path.

GRW-19.title: Weekly digest email renders white-on-white in Gmail mobile dark mode
GRW-19.description: Repro: switch the Gmail mobile app to dark theme and open the weekly digest — body text is white on a white background and unreadable. Roughly a third of digest recipients on iOS are affected. Replace the hardcoded background colors with inline dark-mode-safe styles and add a solid background behind text blocks. Acceptance: render screenshots for Gmail mobile in both light and dark themes show readable text.

CHK-280.title: Coupon codes with trailing whitespace fail validation at checkout
CHK-280.description: Repro: paste 'SAVE10 ' into the coupon field at checkout and the code is rejected as invalid even though SAVE10 is active. Support gets a handful of these weekly, mostly mobile users where the keyboard inserts a space. Strip leading/trailing whitespace and uppercase the input before validating. Acceptance: padded or lowercase variants of a valid code apply correctly, and genuinely invalid codes still show the existing error message.

LED-11.title: Ledger CSV export uses locale decimal separator, breaking finance imports
LED-11.description: Repro: run the ledger CSV export from a browser with a de-DE locale and amounts like 1,234.50 are written as 1.234,50. The finance team's import script then rejects the file or misparses the amounts. The export should always write en-US decimal and thousands separators regardless of the requester's locale, since the import contract specifies that format. Acceptance: an export generated from any locale parses cleanly through the finance import script with matching totals.

PLAT-37.title: Add per-topic consumer lag panels to the Kafka dashboard
PLAT-37.description: The current lag panel shows one aggregate number across all topics, so a single lagging topic hides under healthy ones until alerts fire. This adds per-topic lag graphs for the high-volume topics plus a table of consumer group offsets. Metrics queries are wired up; remaining work is the lag-percentile panel and linking each panel to the owning service's runbook. Acceptance: every high-volume topic has its own lag graph on the Kafka dashboard.

PLAT-13.title: Product cache serves stale prices for hours after catalog edits
PLAT-13.description: Repro: edit a product price in the catalog admin, then load the product page — the old price shows for up to six hours because the cache TTL is 6h and nothing evicts on update. Customers see stale prices and merch has to ask engineering to flush keys manually. Add an eviction call when a product-update event is processed. Acceptance: a price edit is visible on the product page within 60 seconds without any manual flush.

GRW-116.title: Digest scheduler test flakes when run after 23:00 UTC
GRW-116.description: The digest scheduler integration test fails intermittently in evening CI runs: it builds the expected send time from local time while the scheduler uses UTC, so runs after 23:00 UTC cross midnight and the assertion misses by a day. This flake has caused three false broken-build pings this month. Fix by pinning the test clock to a fixed UTC instant instead of wall-clock time. Acceptance: the test passes deterministically no matter when it runs.

PLAT-54.title: Add composite index to speed up monthly statement query on ledger_entries
PLAT-54.description: The monthly statement query filters ledger_entries by account_id and a created_at range and currently takes ~40 seconds on the largest accounts because it scans the full table. This adds a composite index on (account_id, created_at) so the range read uses an index. The migration is validated against a staging copy; remaining work is the production rollout in the low-traffic window and comparing query plans before and after. Acceptance: the statement query completes in under 2 seconds on staging-sized data.

PLAT-132.title: Feature flag admin page needs search and service filter
PLAT-132.description: The flag admin page lists 300+ flags with no search, so finding the right one means scrolling or guessing exact names. Add a text search plus filter dropdowns for service and status (enabled/archived). This is a small frontend change on top of the existing list API, which already supports a query parameter we currently ignore. Acceptance: typing a partial flag name filters the list live, and service plus status filters combine correctly.

PAY-168.title: Log routing decision details for each payment provider selection
PAY-168.description: When a transaction routes to a secondary provider there is no record of why, so support has to ask engineering to trace logs by hand. Add a structured log line at the routing decision point recording the chosen provider, the rule that matched, and the request region. No change to routing behavior itself. Acceptance: any routed transaction can be looked up by transaction ID and the log shows the provider and matching rule.

PAY-365.title: Structured logging for fraud rule declines in fraud-check
PAY-365.description: Currently a rule-based decline logs only the rule name, so support has to pull in engineering to trace any rejection. Repro: trigger a checkout that trips the velocity rule and grep the fraud-check logs — you get 'rule=velocity' with no context. Impact: decline investigations take a day instead of minutes. Done when every decline emits JSON fields for rule name, score, masked card country, and request ID.

PAY-234.title: Map Stripe amount_too_small error to a friendly message in stripe-adapter
PAY-234.description: A €0.30 checkout returns a 500 because stripe-adapter doesn't map Stripe's amount_too_small code. Repro: post a 30-cent payment on staging; the adapter logs an unmapped error and bubbles a generic failure to the user. Impact: micro-amount checkouts show a scary generic error. Acceptance: known Stripe error codes map to friendly messages, with a unit test per code.

LED-251.title: Fix flaky day-boundary test in ledger balance rollup
LED-251.description: The balance rollup suite fails intermittently when run after 23:00 UTC because the day-boundary case depends on the host timezone. Repro: run LedgerBalancesTest with TZ=Australia/Sydney around midnight UTC. Impact: red builds erode trust in CI and mask real regressions. Acceptance: tests use a fixed clock injected via an InstantSupplier so they pass regardless of host timezone.

PLAT-91.title: On-call runbook for slow-query triage on postgres-main
PLAT-91.description: New on-call engineers currently learn slow-query triage on postgres-main by asking around in Slack. Impact: the first half hour of an incident goes to rediscovering where pg_stat_statements lives and how to read it. The runbook should cover finding top queries by time, checking for long-running transactions, and when to escalate. Done when it's reviewed by someone who wasn't involved in writing it.

IDN-250.title: Return 400 with field errors for malformed login payloads in auth
IDN-250.description: POST /login with an email missing '@' or an over-length password returns 500 with a stack trace instead of a 400. Repro: curl the staging auth endpoint with 'not-an-email' as the address. Impact: noisy error alerts and no useful signal for client apps. Done when bean validation returns 400 with per-field messages and integration tests cover the malformed cases.

LED-195.title: Emit duration and skipped-row metrics for the ledger nightly posting job
LED-195.description: The nightly posting job's runtime is invisible until support reports stale balances the next morning. We should emit a duration histogram and a counter for skipped rows from the job, plus a dashboard panel for both. Acceptance: metrics appear on the ledger dashboard after a manual staging run and alerting thresholds can be discussed from real data.

PAY-240.title: Document 422 responses for /refunds in the payments-api OpenAPI spec
PAY-240.description: Generated clients throw on a 422 from /refunds because the OpenAPI spec doesn't declare that response. Repro: generate a client from the current spec and call /refunds with an unknown refund ID. Impact: integrators and our own dashboard treat a documented validation error as unexpected. Done when 422 is declared with the shared error schema and clients regenerate cleanly.

PLAT-194.title: Update postgres-ledger restore runbook with measured drill timings
PLAT-194.description: Last month's restore drill showed the postgres-ledger runbook's 30-minute estimate was optimistic — the actual restore needed an extension reinstall step nobody had documented. This updates the runbook with measured timings per step and a note on the extension gotcha. Done when someone who didn't run the drill walks through the doc and confirms it matches reality.

PLAT-221.title: Fix session TTL mismatch in redis-cache
PLAT-221.description: Session keys in redis-cache expire after 900 seconds while the config declares a 30-minute TTL, so users get logged out about twice as often as intended. Repro: run redis-cli TTL on any session:* key in staging and compare against cache.yaml. Impact: excess re-logins and confused support tickets. Done when TTL matches the declared config and a test asserts the setting is applied.

PLAT-334.title: Audit logging for feature flag toggles
PLAT-334.description: Toggling a flag currently logs only the flag name, so 'who turned this off?' is unanswerable during an incident. This adds a structured audit entry with actor, previous value, new value, and environment for every toggle made through the feature-flags API. Acceptance: a staging toggle produces exactly one audit entry and the flag listing page is unaffected.

LED-78.title: Validate refund amount against remaining refundable balance
LED-78.description: The refunds service currently accepts a refund request for the full order amount even after a partial refund has already been processed, which surfaces later as a cryptic error from the ledger. Repro: create an order, issue a partial refund, then request a refund for the original full amount. This blocks support staff and produces confusing ledger entries. Acceptance: requests exceeding the remaining refundable balance are rejected with a clear 422 message, and unit tests cover partial-refund sequences.

CHK-54.title: Fix layout shift on order history page when status badges load
CHK-54.description: Order rows on the order history page jump a few pixels once the status badges finish loading, which is especially noticeable on slow connections. Repro: throttle the network to Slow 3G and open the order history page. Impact: the page looks broken during load and support has received a handful of 'my orders are missing' reports. Acceptance: badges render inside a reserved-height placeholder so row positions stay stable while loading.

PAY-329.title: Map Stripe decline codes to consistent internal error reasons
PAY-329.description: The adapter currently passes raw Stripe decline codes straight through, so downstream services each do their own string matching against card_declined, insufficient_funds, and so on. Repro: trigger a test-mode payment with a card that returns do_not_honor and inspect the error payload. Impact: error dashboards fragment the same failure into several buckets. Acceptance: every decline code maps to an entry in a single shared enum, unknown codes fall back to a generic value, and unknowns log a warning.

CHK-114.title: Fix stale on-hand quantity shown after warehouse adjustments
CHK-114.description: The inventory detail page sometimes shows an on-hand count that is a few minutes out of date right after a warehouse adjustment is saved, because the cached read only refreshes on a fixed interval. Repro: adjust stock for any SKU, then reload the detail page within 30 seconds. Impact: warehouse staff re-check numbers manually, which slows down cycle counts. Acceptance: the detail page fetches the fresh value on load and the cache is invalidated when an adjustment commits.

CHK-112.title: Reject negative or oversized discount values in pricing rule editor
CHK-112.description: The pricing rule editor accepts negative percentages and values above 100%, which then produce strange line-item amounts until someone notices and disables the rule. Repro: create a percentage discount of -15% or 130% in the editor and run a price calculation with it. Impact: bad rules can reach checkout before anyone catches them. Acceptance: the editor validates the range on save, the API returns a field-level error, and boundary cases are covered by tests.

PLAT-380.title: Add index to support date-range reporting on payments table
PLAT-380.description: The monthly payments report scans the full payments table because no index covers (created_at, status), and the query now takes over two minutes. Repro: run the reporting query from the finance dashboard against staging. Impact: report generation times out during business hours and adds load for other workloads sharing the database. Acceptance: the index ships in a migration, EXPLAIN shows an index scan, and report runtime on staging drops under ten seconds.

PLAT-342.title: Add per-topic consumer lag metrics to the platform dashboard
PLAT-342.description: We only have aggregate consumer lag today, so when one topic falls behind it is hard to tell which pipeline is affected without poking around with CLI tools. Repro: pause a single consumer group in staging and watch the current dashboard. Impact: slower diagnosis whenever a downstream pipeline falls behind. Acceptance: the dashboard shows lag per topic and per consumer group, with alerts wired into the existing on-call thresholds.

GRW-316.title: Fix template rendering for names containing non-ASCII characters
GRW-316.description: Order confirmation emails render the customer name with mojibake when it contains accented characters, because the template engine falls back to a legacy encoding for those templates. Repro: send a test confirmation to an account named 'José García' and inspect the raw email. Impact: looks unprofessional and generates occasional support tickets. Acceptance: all templates declare UTF-8 explicitly, a rendering test covers accented and CJK characters, and a resend of the sample email displays correctly.

LED-299.title: Add trace IDs to ledger entry logs for cross-service debugging
LED-299.description: Ledger entries are logged without any correlation to the originating order or refund, so tracing a discrepancy means grepping by amount and timestamp across services. Repro: post a ledger entry in staging and try to find its source request from the logs alone. Impact: investigations that should take minutes stretch into hours. Acceptance: every ledger write logs the trace ID and source event ID, and the README documents how to join them with order traces.

CHK-29.title: Standardize focus states on checkout form inputs
CHK-29.description: Text inputs on the checkout page show three different focus styles depending on which component was used, and one variant fails contrast checks for keyboard users. Repro: tab through the shipping address form and compare the focus outlines. Impact: a minor accessibility gap flagged in the last design review. Acceptance: all checkout inputs use the shared focus style from the design system, and the form passes the contrast checker.

PLAT-184.title: Validate flag key format on creation in feature-flags service
PLAT-184.description: The admin UI currently accepts flag keys with spaces and uppercase letters, which the SDKs fail to parse until someone renames the flag manually. Repro: create a flag named 'Checkout Redesign v2' and try to evaluate it from the web SDK. Add client- and server-side validation so keys are lowercase kebab-case, max 64 chars, and surface a clear inline error. Acceptance: invalid keys are rejected at the API with a 400 and the UI shows the reason before submit.

GRW-374.title: Stabilize flaky CategoryTreeBuilder test that fails after midnight UTC
GRW-374.description: test_category_tree_sorted_by_date intermittently fails in CI because it builds expected nodes from the local date while the service formats in UTC. Repro: run the suite with TZ=Europe/Berlin late in the day, or with a shuffled test order. Fix the test to freeze time explicitly and assert against UTC-formatted fixtures. Acceptance: 50 consecutive green CI runs and no dependence on execution order.

CHK-119.title: Fix one-cent rounding drift in bulk price export
CHK-119.description: The nightly bulk price export rounds each line independently while the pricing API rounds the computed total, so zero-decimal currencies like JPY came out one unit off. Repro: export prices for a zero-decimal currency and diff against GET /prices. Centralize rounding in a shared helper used by both paths. Acceptance: export and API return identical values for all supported currencies, with unit tests covering zero-decimal cases.

CHK-303.title: Remove layout shift on product detail page when gallery images load
CHK-303.description: Gallery images reserve no height until they load, so the 'Add to cart' button jumps after they resolve — worst on slow mobile connections. Repro: throttle to Slow 3G and open any product with a tall hero image. Reserve aspect-ratio boxes for gallery slots and set explicit width/height attributes. Acceptance: CLS for the page stays under 0.1 in Lighthouse on throttled mobile.

PLAT-383.title: Add partial index to speed up refund lookups in payments schema
PLAT-383.description: The refunds dashboard filters payments by status='refunded' and an updated_at range, and the query was doing a sequential scan, taking 4+ seconds at peak. Repro: run the dashboard query for the last 7 days against staging data. Add a partial index on (updated_at) where status='refunded' and confirm the planner picks it up. Acceptance: dashboard query under 200ms in staging and the slow-query log no longer flags it.

IDN-73.title: Align email verification token expiry with documented 24-hour window
IDN-73.description: Our docs and the verification email both say links are valid for 24 hours, but identity-api actually expires tokens after 60 minutes, so users hit 'link expired' and open support tickets. Repro: request a verification email, wait an hour, click the link. Extend the token TTL to 24h and add a test asserting expiry matches config. Acceptance: a link clicked at hour 23 verifies successfully, and docs need no change.

CHK-341.title: Reject negative and non-numeric prices in bulk CSV import
CHK-341.description: The pricing CSV importer accepts negative amounts and blank values, which published bad prices to two storefront categories before anyone noticed. Repro: import a row with price '-5.00' and watch it go live. Add schema validation that rejects negative, empty, and non-numeric amounts, failing the whole import with a row-level error report. Acceptance: a dry run of a bad file lists offending row numbers and nothing is published.

PLAT-319.title: Backfill currency column on historical ledger_entries rows
PLAT-319.description: ledger_entries.currency was added last month but older rows still have NULL, so finance reports drop those entries when filtering by currency. Repro: run the monthly revenue report for any period before last month and compare against the legacy export. Backfill the ~2.3M affected rows in batches using each account's default currency. Acceptance: zero NULL currency rows in staging after backfill and report totals match the legacy export.

PAY-58.title: Add per-provider latency and error-rate panels to router dashboard
PAY-58.description: When a provider's latency spiked last week, on-call had to grep raw router logs to see which provider was affected because the dashboard only shows aggregate numbers. Repro: simulate elevated latency on a secondary provider in staging and watch the dashboard. Add Grafana panels for p50/p95 latency and error rate grouped by provider, fed by the existing route_completed metric. Acceptance: panels render per provider and match log-derived numbers within 5%.

CHK-368.title: Fix truncated tooltips on the plan comparison table
CHK-368.description: Feature descriptions in the plan comparison table get cut off at roughly 40 characters because the tooltip container has a fixed max-width with overflow hidden, so users can't read what 'Advanced analytics' includes. Repro: hover the third column on the pricing page at 1280px width. Let tooltips wrap at a 280px max-width and add a subtle shadow for legibility. Acceptance: full description visible on hover at 1024px+ widths and in dark mode.

GRW-332.title: Add per-channel send counters to the notifications metrics dashboard
GRW-332.description: The notifications dashboard only showed aggregate send volume, so a delivery dip couldn't be attributed to email, push, or SMS. Added Prometheus counters labeled by channel and template plus a per-channel panel to the dashboard. Cross-checked a week of counters against the delivery events table and they match within 1%. Acceptance: each channel panel updates in near-real-time and the dashboard is linked from the service README.

PLAT-294.title: Write runbook for monthly partition rotation on the postgres-payments event table
PLAT-294.description: The monthly partition rotation on the postgres-payments event table has no documented procedure, and the last rotation was handled ad hoc. Drafting a runbook covering pre-flight checks, the detach/attach sequence, and rollback steps. Currently validating each step against a staging copy of the database. Acceptance: runbook reviewed by a second engineer and merged into the db-runbooks repo before the next rotation window.

GRW-124.title: Fix flaky digest template test that fails near timezone boundaries
GRW-124.description: test_weekly_digest_rendering failed intermittently in CI because it built the 'next Monday' date using the host timezone. Pinned the test clock to a fixed UTC instant and injected it into the template renderer. The test now passes 200 consecutive local runs and three days of clean CI. Acceptance: removed from the flaky-test quarantine list.

IDN-116.title: Show clearer error when password reset link has expired
IDN-116.description: Submitting an expired password reset token returned a generic 'invalid request' with no next step. The reset page now shows 'This link has expired — request a new one' and links directly back to the request form. Added regression tests covering expired, reused, and malformed tokens. Acceptance: verified on staging that all three cases produce the right message.

GRW-24.title: Block duplicate category slugs in the catalog admin form
GRW-24.description: The catalog admin form currently lets you save a category with a slug that already exists, and the public category page then renders whichever row the lookup hits first. Plan is a server-side uniqueness check with an inline error, plus a unique index migration as a backstop. Estimate is a half day including tests. Acceptance: saving a duplicate slug shows the inline error and writes no rows.

PLAT-150.title: Build autovacuum health dashboard for postgres-main
PLAT-150.description: Several large tables on postgres-main went over a week without a successful autovacuum before last month's bloat alert, and we had no standing visibility into it. Building a dashboard with last-run time, dead-tuple ratio, and skipped runs per table. Staging panels are done; the production scrape config is what's left. Acceptance: dashboard covers all user tables on a five-minute refresh.

IDN-311.title: Add machine-readable error codes to identity-api 4xx responses
IDN-311.description: Clients currently distinguish cases like 'unknown email' versus 'locked account' by regex-matching free-form message strings from identity-api 4xx responses. Plan is to add a machine-readable code field with a documented enum while keeping existing messages unchanged for compatibility. Scope covers login, token refresh, and profile endpoints. Acceptance: enum documented in the OpenAPI spec with an example for each code.

PLAT-138.title: Alert on session-cache hit ratio drops in redis-cache
PLAT-138.description: A miss spike on the session cache explained a recent latency bump, but we only found it by digging through redis-cli by hand. Added hit/miss ratio panels per cache instance plus an alert when the 15-minute ratio drops below 80%. Verified the alert path by forcing misses against staging. Acceptance: alert fires with the instance label and routes to the platform channel.

GRW-359.title: Fix quiet-hours timezone bug in push notification scheduling
GRW-359.description: Quiet hours for push notifications were computed in UTC, so the 10pm mute window landed at the wrong hour for most users outside the server timezone. Fixed the scheduler to use the recipient's profile timezone with a UTC fallback and added tests across a DST boundary. Confirmed on staging profiles in three timezones. Acceptance: no push is delivered inside a user's local quiet window.

PLAT-107.title: Regenerate schema docs for the postgres-ledger tables
PLAT-107.description: The ledger schema docs were several migrations out of date, which kept tripping up anyone writing analytics queries against postgres-ledger. Regenerated the docs from migration history and added short descriptions for the tables that lacked them. Published the result to the internal data handbook and linked it from the service README. Acceptance: doc generation runs as a CI job so it can't drift again.
